notes.meaning: The physical skies and heavens constantly show the power, wisdom, and majesty of God their Maker. Just by existing in all their beauty and orderly arrangement, they announce God's creative work to everyone below. Looking up at the vastness above reminds us that God is great, powerful, and good.

Day and night take turns speaking about God like an overflowing fountain that never stops running. One day passes the message to the next, and each starry night reveals knowledge of the Creator to the night that follows. Time never interrupts this steady witness to God's greatness.

The skies do not use human speech, audible words, or a spoken language. Even so, their silent message is understood everywhere on earth. Creation speaks directly to human eyes and minds without making a sound.

The silent witness of creation travels over the entire globe so that no nation is left without it. In the open skies, God set up a place for the sun to dwell, as if pitching a tent for it. From there, the sun brings light to the whole world.

The rising sun is compared to a bridegroom stepping out of his bridal room, dressed in bright, joyful clothes on his wedding day. It is also like a strong athlete or champion, eager and full of energy to run a long race. This picture shows the beauty, joy, and vigorous strength that God built into the natural world.

The sun travels across the whole sky, moving from one end of the horizon all the way to the other. Nothing on earth is hidden from its penetrating heat and light. In the same way, God's warmth and governing care reach into every part of life.

God's written Word is completely perfect, reviving and restoring the soul by turning people away from sin and back to God. His reliable teachings give steady guidance that makes simple, teachable people wise. While nature shows God's power, His written instruction brings people into a personal relationship with Him.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest that the sharp shift in tone, rhythm, and subject matter between verse 6 and verse 7 indicates two originally separate poems were joined together here.

notes.meaning: God's directions set out straight, upright paths, which bring deep gladness and peace to the heart. His commands are bright and clear, giving moral light to our eyes so we can see how to live rightly.

The fear of the Lord means reverent, worshipful trust that hates evil, and the Word that teaches this holy worship is completely pure. Because it is free from all error, it never decays and stands firm forever. God's rulings and decisions are always fair, reliable, and completely just.

God's teachings are far more valuable than the finest pure gold, offering riches that earthly wealth cannot buy. They are also sweeter and more satisfying to the inner person than fresh honey dripping straight from the comb. Those who love God find true delight in what He says.

God's Word warns His servants against dangerous paths and the painful traps of sin. Obeying His commands brings a great reward, both in the present peace of a clear conscience and in eternal blessings to come.

Looking into God's holy standard makes people see how easily they wander off the right path. No one can track or understand all their own mistakes, because many sins are forgotten or committed without realizing it. David therefore asks God to forgive and wash him clean from these hidden faults.

David prays for God to hold him back from willful sins—wrongs done intentionally with a proud and defiant attitude. He asks that such deliberate habits may never rule over his life or make him their slave. With God's restraining help, a believer is protected from falling into great rebellion against Him.

David asks that both the spoken words of his mouth and the quiet thoughts of his heart be pleasing to God, like an acceptable sacrifice. He trusts in the Lord as his Rock, which means his solid foundation and shelter. He also calls God his Redeemer, the loving family protector who rescues His people from danger and bondage.
